newsitem.title: ISRAEL: ISRAELI UNLINKED BONDS END HIGHER.
newsitem.headline: ISRAELI UNLINKED BONDS END HIGHER.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed hardly changed on Sunday with prices of unlinked bonds and Makams rising in what traders said was a technical correction.
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.07 pct to 108.57
Volume including Makams was a high 214 million shekels.

"We saw high demand for unlinked bonds and Makams today as these bonds fell sharply during the last few trading days on expectations of a relatively high July consumer price index," said Michael Politzer, head of the economics department at the Central Securities Corp.
"During the last three weeks yields on the (one year) Makam rose from 12.8 percent to 13.2 percent and today we saw a slight correction," said Ron Weisberg at I.B.I Investment House.
He added that trading volume of the Makam was relatively high at 99 million shekels.
Politzer added that yields of 13.5 percent on unlinked bonds are still attractive for some investors.

The rise of the dollar against the shekel in June, which caused June's CPI to rise a steep 1.1 percent, has triggered fears of a series of high indices. July's CPI, to be published on August 15, is also feared to be a high one percent, some traders have said.

Trading in CPI-linked bonds was mixed with a slight rise in short bonds and a mild decline in long bonds. "Long bonds were expected to fall because they made a very big move and yields fell sharply, but because of the expected tight supply of these bonds they closed only slightly lower," Politzer said.

Government bond redemptions are expected to total about four billion shekels in August against issues of 1.6 billion shekels; a successful privatisation process and higher tax revenues are all expected to lessen the government's need to raise debt on the bond market.
Dollar-linked bonds fell sharply following the recent rise of the shekel against the dollar.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
- Dan Gerstenfeld, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 x233
